title: Rubio says Ukraine hit ships tied to U.S. oil interests
excerpt: Marco Rubio accused Ukraine of striking ships carrying American-owned energy products in the Black Sea in comments reported by the New York Post. He separately said the Trump administration had not paused intelligence-sharing with Kyiv.
body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio accused Ukraine of attacking ships carrying American-owned energy products in the Black Sea, according to the New York Post’s account of an interview released Sunday. The same report said Rubio also told reporters Monday in Uzbekistan that the Trump administration had not paused intelligence-sharing meant to warn Kyiv about Russian ballistic missile attacks.

In the interview the Post said was released Sunday, Rubio said, “We have seen strikes on energy vessels in the Black Sea. And there’s been complaints, a lot, because we have American companies calling us and saying, ‘Hey, that was our oil on that ship that was hit by Ukraine.’” He added, “Now, I don’t believe Ukraine intentionally targeted them, but those ships got hit.”

Rubio’s Monday comments in Uzbekistan were about a different subject. According to the New York Post, he responded to Zelensky’s complaint about intelligence sharing by saying, “There’s been no pause. Zelensky should be focused on bringing an end to this war.”

The separate timing matters because Rubio’s ship allegation did not come in the same setting as his Monday remarks. The supplied reporting shows the Black Sea comment was made in a separate interview, while the Uzbekistan exchange addressed whether Washington had cut off intelligence support.

ABC News reported on Sept. 22 that Rubio had made a similar accusation in a Fox News interview, saying that “over the last few months, on a number of occasions, American-linked ships, American oil supplies have been targeted, probably not deliberately, but targeted nonetheless by Ukraine.” ABC said it was not immediately clear what specific incidents he meant.

The outlet also noted that Ukraine had conducted strikes on the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiysk, which contains export facilities for the Caspian Pipeline Consortium. ABC said the consortium counts Chevron and ExxonMobil among its top shareholders.

Kyiv Post likewise reported that Rubio did not publicly name the vessels or clarify whether they were American-owned, U.S.-flagged or tied to the United States through cargo, chartering or energy infrastructure. The outlet said the claim appeared to refer to vessels using Russia’s Black Sea ports to transport oil connected to the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, which carries Kazakh crude.

The available reporting does not identify the ships Rubio had in mind or establish that the vessels were U.S.-flagged or owned. It does show that Rubio has repeatedly raised the issue of attacks affecting energy shipping and oil infrastructure with American links, while also arguing that the United States has not stopped helping Kyiv track Russian missile threats.

fc.summary: No factual issues were found against the supplied source excerpts. The article correctly distinguishes Rubio's Sunday-released Breitbart interview from his Monday remarks in Uzbekistan and accurately attributes the ABC News and Kyiv Post reporting.

summary.summary: Reworked the lead to match the published headline and the supplied New York Post reporting, while keeping the earlier Fox News comment as context. Tightened attribution, removed unsupported repetition, and ended on the unresolved question of which ships and cargoes Rubio meant.
